questions.title: Homeostasis: receptor detects change and sends message to control center
questions.question: Regarding Homeostasis mechanism, which of the following detects change and sends a message to the control center:

explanations.A: Correct. In a homeostatic control system, the receptor is the component that detects the change, the stimulus, in the internal environment. It then sends that information onward as a message to the control centre. The control centre is what then coordinates the appropriate response, downstream of the receptor's own detecting role.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The stimulus is the change itself that occurs in the internal environment, not the component that detects it and reports it onward -- that detecting-and-reporting role belongs to the receptor.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The effector is the component that carries out the response at the end of the control loop, not the component that first detects the change.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The response is the effector's output, the last step of the loop, not the detection step this question asks about.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the receptor as the component of a homeostatic control system that detects a change and sends a message to the control centre.

questions.title: Homeostasis: control center receives message and coordinates response
questions.question: Regarding Homeostasis mechanism, which of the following receives the message and coordinates a response:

explanations.A: Correct. The control centre is the component of the homeostatic loop that receives the message sent by the receptor. It then coordinates the response, typically by determining an appropriate output. That output is directed to the effector, which carries the response out.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The effector is the component that carries out the coordinated response, downstream of the control centre, not the component that receives the receptor's message and does the coordinating.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The response is the outcome the effector produces, not the coordinating step performed by the control centre.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Homeostasis is the overall goal of the whole system, keeping the internal environment constant, not a single named component of the control loop.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the control centre as the component that receives the receptor's message and coordinates the response.

questions.title: Homeostasis: effector responds to output from the control center
questions.question: Regarding Homeostasis mechanism , which of the following responds to the output from the control center

explanations.A: Incorrect. The stimulus is the original change that started the loop, upstream of the control centre's output, not the component that responds to that output.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The receptor is the component that detects the original stimulus and reports it, upstream of the control centre, not the component that acts on its output.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The response is the outcome the effector produces, the result of the effector acting on the control centre's output, not the component itself that responds to it.
explanations.D: Correct. The effector is the component of the homeostatic loop that responds to the output from the control centre. It carries out the actual action, such as a muscle contracting or a gland secreting. This action is what produces the corrective response the whole loop was aiming for.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the effector as the component that responds to the control centre's output, producing the corrective response.

questions.title: Positive feedback increases or speeds up the original change
questions.question: Regarding Homeostasis mechanism, which of the following Increases or speeds up original change

explanations.A: Incorrect. Negative feedback drives a response that reverses or stops the original change, moving the variable back toward its original value, the opposite of amplifying it.
explanations.B: Correct. Positive feedback makes the response progressively larger, amplifying rather than reversing the original change. The body uses positive feedback in a few specific processes that need to accelerate to completion rapidly, such as blood clotting and uterine contractions during childbirth, rather than as the general mechanism of homeostatic regulation.
explanations.C: Incorrect. "Involuntary control" is not itself the term for the amplifying, self-accelerating loop this question describes -- that specific pattern is positive feedback.
explanations.D: Incorrect. "Voluntary control" describes control under conscious direction, not the automatic, self-accelerating amplification this question describes, which is positive feedback.

questions.learning_objective: Identify positive feedback as the mechanism that increases or speeds up the original change.

questions.title: Negative feedback tries to reverse or stop the original change
questions.question: Regarding Homeostasis mechanism, which of the following tries to reverse or stops the original change

explanations.A: Correct. Negative feedback is the mechanism almost all homeostatic control systems use. The response it drives works to reverse or stop the original change. This brings the regulated variable back toward its original value, which is exactly the corrective logic homeostasis depends on.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Positive feedback amplifies the original change rather than reversing it, the opposite pattern from what this question describes.
explanations.C: Incorrect. "Involuntary control" is not itself the term for the corrective, change-reversing loop this question describes -- that specific pattern is negative feedback.
explanations.D: Incorrect. "Voluntary control" describes control under conscious direction, not the automatic, change-reversing correction this question describes, which is negative feedback.

questions.learning_objective: Identify negative feedback as the mechanism that tries to reverse or stop the original change, the pattern almost all homeostatic systems use.

questions.title: Keeping the internal body environment constant is homeostasis
questions.question: keeping the internal body environment constant is the ……..:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Haemostasis is the process of stopping bleeding (clot formation and vascular/platelet responses), a different word that sounds similar but names an unrelated process.
explanations.B: Correct. Homeostasis is the term for keeping the conditions of the internal environment constant. Almost all body systems work toward this goal, mainly through negative feedback control loops, and failure of homeostasis often leads to disease or death.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Haemolysis is the destruction (rupture) of red blood cells, an unrelated process to the constancy of the internal environment.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Feedback is one of the mechanisms (alongside the receptor-control centre-effector loop) that homeostasis uses to achieve constancy, but it is not itself the name for the overall goal of keeping the internal environment constant -- that name is homeostasis.

questions.learning_objective: State that keeping the internal body environment constant is the definition of homeostasis.
